## The problem

<!--
Start here, and be concrete. What were you trying to do, and what happened
instead? A real moment where the tool failed you is worth more than a feature
description — it often points at a better solution than the one either of us
would have thought of first.

Good:  "I knew I'd discussed Postgres connection pooling but I'd talked about
        it with both Claude and ChatGPT, and I couldn't search across both."
Less good:  "Add multi-provider support."
-->

## Proposed solution

<!-- What you think should happen. Rough is fine. -->

## Alternatives considered

<!--
What else would solve your problem? Including "I currently work around it by
..." — a workaround tells us how much friction there really is, and sometimes
the workaround is good enough that the feature is not worth its complexity.
-->

## Scope check

<!-- Tick what applies. -->

- [ ] I have read the [roadmap](../../ROADMAP.md) and this is not already planned
- [ ] This works without any conversation data leaving the user's machine
- [ ] This does not require a new heavy runtime dependency
- [ ] I would be interested in implementing this

<!--
The second box matters most. Local-first is the whole point of the project,
and a feature that needs a cloud service will be declined no matter how good
it is. See "Not planned" in the roadmap.

The third is softer, but the dependency list is short on purpose — every
addition is something a user has to install to read their own chat logs.
-->
